newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian defence efficiency review delayed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian defence efficiency review delayed.

text.p: Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said on Thursday the political crisis in neighbouring Papua New Guinea had delayed Canberra's planned release of a defence efficiency report.
McLachlan said in a statement the government was too busy with other issues to fully discuss the review into defence management and financial practices until early April.
The review, part of a comprehensive study of Australia's defence organisations and policies ordered by the year-old conservative government, was originally due to be released at the end of March.
Australian government and military chiefs are closely monitoring the situation in Papua New Guinea, where looting and lawlessness have followed a row between elements of the army and the government.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan this week sacked defence chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok after the general urged Chan's removal over a plan to use mercenaries to quell an island rebellion.
Singirok has accepted his sacking, but supporters of the popular general have not and have demanded senior members of the South Pacific nation's government stand down.

Australia, a close neighbour of Papua New Guinea and its biggest aid donor, has opposed Port Moresby's use of mercenaries to end the nine-year secessionist rebellion on Bougainville island, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby.
